pass_a_gloss: Neither then must one deny the son of God nor be shamed of him or of his household ones or of his words, but one must hear this: whoever denies me in front of the humans, I also will deny him in front of my father in the heavens; and this: for whoever is shamed of me and my own, this one the son of the human will be shamed of, whenever he comes in the glory of him and of the father and of the holy messengers; and this: for whoever is shamed of me and my words in the adulterous and sinning generation, the son of the human also will be shamed of him, whenever he comes in the glory of the father with the holy messengers. And Jesus too at one time stood under a stake, having looked down on shame, and through this took his seat on the right of God; and his copiers, looking down on shame, will be seated along with him and will be kings along with him in the heavens, with the one who came to throw a peace not upon the land but upon the soul of his learners, and to throw a blade upon the land. For since the word of God is alive and at work and cutting more than every two mouthed blade and going through up to a parting of soul and breath, of joints and of marrows, and fit to judge the musings and notions of a heart, this one most of all now acts as umpire for our souls with the peace that rises above every mind, which he let go to his apostles, but threw a blade between the likeness of the dusty one and that of the one above the heavens; in order that, taking over for the present the one of us above the heavens, afterwards, us having become worthy of not being chopped in two, he may make us out of wholes heavenly. And not only a blade did he come to throw upon the land but also a fire, about which he says: I wish if already it were lit. Let this fire therefore be lit also in you, blotting out every earthy and body fond reckoning of yours; and the dipping about which Jesus was held tight until it is completed, with all forwardness be dipped now. And you, the one having a wife and children and brothers and sisters, bear in mind this: if someone comes toward me and does not hate the father and the mother and the wife and the children and the brothers and the sisters, he cannot be my learner; and both of you, this: if someone comes toward me and does not hate, in addition to the earlier ones, still also his own soul, he cannot be my learner. But so hate your own soul as through the hating to guard it into life of ages; for the one hating, he says, his own soul in this world guards it into life of ages. Therefore hate the soul through the life of ages, being convinced that a fine and useful hate Jesus teaches to hate. And as on behalf of the soul being guarded into life of ages it will be needful for us to hate it, thus hate wife and children and brothers and sisters, you who have these, so that you may help those being hated, through the very having hated taking up openness toward doing them good, having become a friend to God.
pass_b_english: So we must neither deny the Son of God nor be ashamed of him, or of his own people, or of his words. We must listen to this: “Whoever denies me before men, I too will deny him before my Father who is in heaven” (Matthew 10:33); and to this: “For whoever is ashamed of me and of mine, of him the Son of Man will be ashamed when he comes in his glory and that of the Father and of the holy angels” (Luke 9:26); and to this: “For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in the adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man too will be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of the Father with the holy angels” (Mark 8:38).

Jesus too once “endured a cross, despising shame”, and for this reason “sat down at the right hand” of God (Hebrews 12:2). His imitators too, despising shame, will sit with him and reign with him in heaven: with him who came to cast peace not “on the earth” but on the soul of his own disciples, and to cast “a sword” “on the earth” (Matthew 10:34). For since “the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing as far as the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart” (Hebrews 4:12), this Word now above all bestows on our souls the peace that surpasses all understanding (Philippians 4:7), which he left to his apostles (John 14:27); but he has cast a sword between the image of the earthy one and that of the heavenly one (1 Corinthians 15:49), so that, taking to himself for the present the heavenly one in us, he may later, when we have become worthy not to be cut in two, make us wholly heavenly.

He came to cast not only “a sword” “on the earth”, but also “fire”, of which he says, “How I wish it were already kindled!” (Luke 12:49). So let this fire be kindled in you too, wiping out every earthly and body-loving thought of yours; and be baptized now, with all eagerness, with the baptism by which Jesus “was hard pressed until it was accomplished” (Luke 12:50).

And you who have “a wife and children and brothers and sisters”, remember: “If anyone comes to me and does not hate father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, he cannot be my disciple” (Luke 14:26). And both of you, remember: “If anyone comes to me and does not hate”, besides the former, “his own soul as well, he cannot be my disciple”. But hate your own soul in such a way that by hating it you keep it for eternal life. “For the one who hates”, he says, “his own soul in this world keeps it for eternal life” (John 12:25). So hate your soul for the sake of eternal life, persuaded that the hatred Jesus teaches you to hate with is good and profitable. And just as we shall have to hate the soul so that it may be kept for eternal life, so you who have them, hate “wife and children and brothers and sisters”, so that you may benefit those you hate: through the very fact of having hated them you gain boldness to do them good, once you have become a friend of God.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 37); the old English was a digest. It dropped the three quotations on denial and shame, added 'for the joy set before him' (not in Origen's text), invented 'dividing son from father', 'hating lawfully what hinders godliness' and 'perfect love', and dropped the peace of the apostles and the benefit to the hated family.

Read og as ὃς, ἐλθόντε as ἐλθόντι, δικνούμενος &; as διικνούμενος, κρετικὸς as κριτικός, ἔτε as ἔτι, Ἅ8 as ὁ, ınv as τήν, ζωὴ» as ζωήν, εὐπὲρ as ὑπέρ, 6 ἔχων as ὁ ἔχων, di as δι᾽; '115' and '1:20' are line numbers.
Koetschau prints ἡμῶν (Wettstein, Delarue; MSS ὑμῶν); masculine 'the heavenly one in us', with no noun supplied.
'bestows on' (awards, arbitrates); the sense of giving the peace is kept without adding 'rule'.
Rendered as a wish, 'How I wish it were already kindled!', the usual sense of θέλω εἰ.
